In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the light emission of LEDs was dominated by the bandgap emission of ZnO and the Ga-O interdiffusion emission.
the red emission from the annealed-ZnO/pGaN heterostructure LEDs was attributed to the interdiffusion of Ga and O at the n-Zno/p-GaN interface and the formation of a Ga-O interlayer.

the EL from the 450°C-annealed n-ZnO/GaOx/p-GaN heterostructure LED was attributed to intrinsic transitions between the n-Zn0 and p-GaN bandgap, and the EL from the LEDs annealed at higher temperature was attributed to interdiffusion and formation of Ga-O interlayer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the EL from the annealed-ZnO-GaN LEDs was dominated by the intrinsic transitions between the n-Zn-O and p-GaN bands, which were influenced by the interdiffusion at their interface.
a post-annealed process at a temperature of ~800 °C could effectively improve the crystallinity of n-ZnOnanocrystalline and p-GaN films, and hence, the EL efficiency.
the annealing temperature and ambient gas were the main factors for determining the light emission of the n-Zn0/p-GaN heterostructure LEDs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the post-annealing treatment can effectively improve the electrical and optical properties of the ZnO/GaN LED.
the EL of an n-Zo/p-GaN heterostructure LED can be modulated through post-annealing treatment, which is attributed to the interdiffusion at its interface.
the EL spectra from the n-Zn-O/p-GaN heterostructure LEDs annealed under different atmospheres can be explained by the interfacial reactions and the interdiffusion between the n-Zn0 and p-GaN.
